title: Altinn Studio — Operator
description: The runtime operator (service operator), one per service owner cluster, across the runtime environments. Its controllers run in the elected leader: Maskinporten clients and their key rotation, secret and app code sync, Key Vault sync, Grafana alert routing, CNPG databases and, outside prod, the inactivity scaler. Runs, failures and their duration per controller come from altinn.operator.run.duration (one point per reconcile or pass of a periodic sync, with error.type for a failed one); Maskinporten client states, the inactivity state and leadership from the operator's gauges; outgoing calls from http.client.request.duration; versions and process starts from altinn.workload.start_time. All from altinn-studio-metrics, which isn't sampled. Below, for triage, the failed runs from their traces: tail sampling keeps every trace with an error. Service owner comes from altinn.service_owner, which the router in each service owner cluster sets on the resource. Rates use increase_pure() over $__rate_interval divided by its length rather than rate(), so a first failure on a new series shows. Blue markers are each version's first start per environment (90 days of history), orange markers each process start (off by default).

list.name: Deploys (first start of version)
list.textFormat: {{deployment.environment.name}}. Earliest retained process start for this version in the selected clusters (90d history). An upgrade rolls out ring by ring, so later clusters start it later.

panels.title: Operators reporting
panels.description: Operator processes with an altinn.workload.start_time sample in the last minute at the range end, per environment. One per service owner cluster normally, two during a rollout. Counts processes exporting telemetry, not readiness.

panels.title: Clusters without a leader
panels.description: Service owner clusters whose operator processes report altinn.operator.leader, none of them 1, at the range end. Only the elected leader runs the controllers, so these clusters run none. A process reports 0 until it is elected; a value here that lasts more than a minute or two is a stuck election.

panels.title: Failed runs
panels.description: Controller runs that failed over the time range: reconciles and passes of the periodic syncs whose span has error.type. From altinn.operator.run.duration, which isn't sampled.

panels.title: Maskinporten clients not ready
panels.description: MaskinportenClients whose Ready condition is False at the range end, from altinn.operator.maskinporten.clients. Their apps can't get Maskinporten tokens. See the Maskinporten row for which clusters.

panels.title: Operators by service owner
panels.description: One row per service owner cluster at the range end: the operator version it runs (service.version, the commit), how many processes report, whether one is the elected leader, and when the oldest of them started.

panels.title: Clusters by operator version
panels.description: Service owner clusters running each operator version (service.version), stacked. An upgrade rolls out ring by ring through the upgrade channels, so a new version's band grows in steps as each ring's tag moves.

panels.title: Runs per second by controller
panels.description: Controller runs per second: reconciles of the event-driven controllers (maskinporten, secretsync, appcodesync) and passes of the periodic syncs, from altinn.operator.run.duration. Select a series to search that controller's traces.

panels.title: Failed runs per second by controller and error type
panels.description: Failed runs per second by controller and error.type, the step that failed (get_source_secret, ensure_helm_release, update_status, …). Select a series to search the failed traces; tail sampling keeps every trace with an error.

panels.title: Run duration (p95) by controller
panels.description: 95th percentile run duration per controller, from altinn.operator.run.duration's buckets (5 ms to 60 s). A periodic sync's run covers all its work in one pass, such as every mapping or every app.

panels.title: Failed runs by service owner
panels.description: Failed runs over the time range by service owner, controller and error.type. Complete: from the metric, not from sampled traces.

panels.title: Stalled periodic syncs
panels.description: Periodic syncs (grafanapolicysync, cnpgsync, inactivityscaler, azurekeyvaultsync) that completed a run in the last 7 days but none without an error in the last 30 minutes, per service owner. They poll every 5 to 10 minutes, so 30 minutes is several missed passes: the sync fails every time or has stopped. A sync that isn't enabled in a cluster never runs there and isn't listed.

panels.title: Maskinporten clients by state
panels.description: MaskinportenClients across the selected clusters by their Ready condition: ready, not_ready (the last reconcile failed) or unknown (not reconciled yet). From altinn.operator.maskinporten.clients, which only the leader reports.

panels.title: Clusters with clients not ready
panels.description: Service owner clusters with MaskinportenClients that aren't ready at the range end. The failed reconciles and their error types are in Failed runs by service owner (controller maskinporten) and in the traces below.

panels.title: Outgoing calls per second by host
panels.description: The operator's HTTP calls per second by server.address: the Kubernetes API, Maskinporten, the Grafana API and the org registry. Kubernetes watches aren't counted: they're long-lived connections.

panels.title: Failed outgoing calls per second by host
panels.description: Calls per second that failed, by host and by status code (a 4xx or 5xx response) or error.type (a transport error, such as net.OpError for a refused connection or a timeout). The Kubernetes API's 404 and 409 are often expected: a deleted object, or an update conflict that is retried.

panels.title: Outgoing call latency (p95) by host
panels.description: 95th percentile time to the response headers per host.

panels.title: Clusters by inactivity state
panels.description: Non-prod clusters by the state the inactivity scaler last applied, stacked: normal, ttd_offhours (ttd's apps scaled down outside working hours), no_apps (no apps deployed, the gateway and pdf3 relay scaled down) or both. From altinn.operator.inactivityscaler.state; the scaler doesn't run in prod.

panels.title: Inactivity state by service owner
panels.description: The state each cluster's inactivity scaler last applied at the range end, and whether an override (the inactivity-scaler-override ConfigMap) forced it.

panels.title: Failed runs (traces)
panels.description: Failed controller runs per second, from their entry spans with status error. Tail sampling keeps every trace with an error, so this is complete; each dot is an example trace to open.

panels.title: Failures by controller, error type and object
panels.description: Failed runs over the time range by controller, error.type and the Kubernetes object the run worked on, from the stored spans (altinn-studio-traces-logsql). Complete, as tail sampling keeps every failed trace.

panels.title: Recent failed runs
panels.description: The latest failed controller runs with the status description (the error message), newest first. Select a trace to open it; the operator's ERROR logs for the run are linked from the trace.

targets.expr: {resource_attr:service.name="operator"} "resource_attr:deployment.environment.name":$env "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner":$service_owner "span_attr:altinn.operator.controller":* status_code:2 | sort by (_time desc) limit 200 | fields _time, "resource_attr:altinn.service_owner", name, "span_attr:error.type", status_message, "span_attr:altinn.app", "span_attr:altinn.operator.object.name", duration, trace_id | rename trace_id as trace
